title: Portland rain or shine
summary: Seven days of food carts and doughnuts, roses and a Japanese garden, books and coffee, and waterfalls in the Columbia River Gorge.
author: friends of Placemoir

places.name: The Benson Portland
places.notes: A 1913 hotel with a walnut-paneled lobby, where presidents stay when they're in town.

places.name: Hotel deLuxe
places.notes: Old-Hollywood glamour and the Driftwood Room bar, on the edge of downtown.

places.name: The Hoxton, Portland
places.notes: Stylish, fairly priced rooms across from the Chinese garden, with a rooftop bar.

places.name: Jupiter Hotel
places.notes: A retro motor lodge turned hip hotel on the east side. Ask for a quiet room away from the courtyard.

places.name: Le Pigeon
places.notes: French food with Portland nerve, at a counter facing the cooks. Order the burger if it's on.

places.name: Canard
places.notes: Le Pigeon's casual sibling. Duck-stack pancakes at brunch, and the steamburger.

places.name: Screen Door
places.notes: Southern cooking with a famous fried chicken and waffle brunch. Get there early.

places.name: Kachka
places.notes: Russian dumplings, zakuski and house-infused vodkas. A party of a dinner.

places.name: Nong's Khao Man Gai
places.notes: One perfect Thai dish, poached chicken and rice with a ginger-chili sauce. From a food cart to a café.

places.name: Ken's Artisan Pizza
places.notes: Wood-fired pizza in a lively room. Arrive at opening or put your name in and wait at a bar nearby.

places.name: Ava Gene's
places.notes: Roman-style cooking with Oregon vegetables. A Division Street favorite.

places.name: Tusk
places.notes: Bright Middle Eastern plates and a sunny patio.

places.name: Lardo
places.notes: Big, messy sandwiches. The pork meatball banh mi and the dirty fries.

places.name: Voodoo Doughnut
places.notes: The pink-box tourist classic. Get the Bacon Maple Bar, once.

places.name: Blue Star Donuts
places.notes: Brioche doughnuts for grown-ups. Blueberry bourbon basil is the one.

places.name: Salt & Straw
places.notes: Strange and wonderful ice cream flavors. Ask to taste a few before you choose.

places.name: Stumptown Coffee Roasters
places.notes: The roaster that put Portland coffee on the map, with its downtown café a few blocks from Powell's.

places.name: Coava Coffee Roasters
places.notes: Bright, clean coffee in a big, airy room shared with a woodshop.

places.name: Multnomah Whiskey Library
places.notes: Over 1,500 spirits on rolling ladders. Book a seat; it's worth it.

places.name: Deschutes Brewery Portland Public House
places.notes: The Bend brewery's big Pearl District pub, with Portland-only beers on tap.

places.name: Powell's City of Books
places.notes: A whole city block of new and used books. Grab a map at the door and find the Rare Book Room.

places.name: Lan Su Chinese Garden
places.notes: A walled Ming-style garden in the middle of the city. Have tea in the teahouse.

places.name: Portland Art Museum
places.notes: The oldest art museum in the Northwest, with strong Native American and Northwest galleries.

places.name: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry
places.notes: Hands-on science on the river, and a real Navy submarine to tour.

places.name: Pittock Mansion
places.notes: A 1914 French Renaissance mansion with a view of five Cascade peaks on a clear day.

places.name: Portland Saturday Market
places.notes: A big outdoor craft market by the river, on weekends from March to Christmas.

places.name: Pioneer Courthouse Square
places.notes: Portland's living room, with bricks bearing donors' names and the weather machine at noon.

places.name: Portland Aerial Tram
places.notes: A four-minute ride up to Marquam Hill with views of Mount Hood. Ride down for free.

places.name: Portland Japanese Garden
places.notes: One of the finest Japanese gardens outside Japan. Go when it opens, and in October for the maples.

places.name: International Rose Test Garden
places.notes: Ten thousand rose bushes and a view of Mount Hood. Free, and at its peak in June.

places.name: Forest Park
places.notes: Over 80 miles of trails in one of the largest urban forests in the country. Start on the Lower Macleay Trail.

places.name: Tom McCall Waterfront Park
places.notes: A riverside promenade with cherry trees in spring. Loop across the bridges on the Eastbank Esplanade.

places.name: Mt. Tabor Park
places.notes: A park on a dormant volcano, with old reservoirs and sunset views over downtown.

places.name: Laurelhurst Park
places.notes: A classic Olmsted-style park with a duck pond and huge old trees.

places.name: Multnomah Falls
places.address: 53000 E Historic Columbia River Hwy, Bridal Veil, OR 97010
places.notes: A 620-foot waterfall 40 minutes east. A timed permit may be needed in summer, so check before you go.

places.name: Haystack Rock
places.notes: A day trip to the coast. Tide pools with sea stars and puffins in spring and summer.
